messages:
customer_jones: Hey team, embeddings are failing for us in prod after the SDK upgrade. Getting a hard error: "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 768". This started after we moved to @redwood-embeddings-js v1.4.0. Our payloads are unchanged.

alex_s: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact request body (no secrets) and the SDK call? also which model are you calling?

customer_jones: model: text-embedding-3-large, code (TS):

```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood-embeddings-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'text-embedding-3-large', input: ['doc1', 'doc2'] });
```

and the error we get from our server: 

```
ERROR: embeddings call failed: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 768 (request_id=req_0a1b2c3d)
```

nidhi: thanks. two quick things to rule out: 1) are you accidentally hitting the small model (768-dim) via routing? 2) do you have any client-side transformation (e.g., downcasting floats, slicing arrays)?

customer_jones: we pinned model param to text-embedding-3-large everywhere. no transformations on our side. this started exactly after upgrading the TS SDK. we did notice the SDK now has a batching layer by default (batchSize: 8).

ryan_m: @nidhi @alex_s fyi: I recall a recent change where the JS SDK started converting Float64 to Float32 for network perf and there was one edge-case where it serialized embeddings as base64 of 32-bit arrays and the server expected 64-bit? could cause length mismatch if bytes interpreted differently.

eng-ml: assigning to us to investigate. customer, can you share the request_id from the error (you included one) and a HAR/export showing the raw HTTP body? we'll check what the server actually received. Also what's your region?

customer_jones: request_id=req_0a1b2c3d, region=us-east-1. attaching a small curl repro:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-large","input":["test"]}'
```

This curl returns a valid 1536-dim vector. So the raw HTTP path is fine. That points to the SDK client shipping a transformed payload.

support-bot: :eyes: Logged ticket RT-4572, severity=P2. Notifying eng-ml and devex.

alex_s: thanks for the curl test — that isolates it. can you also run the ts SDK with DEBUG env var to see the serialized payload? e.g., DEBUG=redwood:* node repro.js

customer_jones: debug log shows payload with base64 encoded "vectors" field and length 6144 bytes (which matches 1536*4), but server read it as 768*4 bytes. seems like server decoded as 768 floats.

nidhi: hypothesis: the JS SDK is setting model override to text-embedding-3-small for some batched subrequest or using the wrong model in the per-batch metadata. Or server-side model routing is picking a smaller variant due to a compatibility matrix bug when clients include a legacy header.

ryan_m: I dug into the SDK change: v1.4.0 introduced a batching proxy that sends a multiple-inputs envelope. It includes a per-input "model_hint" field which should be carried through. There's an off-by-one bug in the envelope where the hint for the first item is dropped, causing the cluster to fallback to the default smaller embedder for that batch. That would explain why our curl works but batched SDK calls hit the small model.

eng-ml: confirmed in logs for req_0a1b2c3d: backend selected model text-embedding-3-small for subrequest index 0; selection reason: missing model_hint. We have the SDK envelope shape mismatch.

alex_s: mitigation for customer: set the SDK option batchSize: 1 or disable client-side batching until patch. Also set request timeout higher if you see retries. Example:

```ts
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'text-embedding-3-large', input: [...], batchSize: 1, timeout: 60000 });
```

customer_jones: can do. how urgent is a patch? this breaks our accuracy.

eng-ml: we'll ship a hotfix to the JS SDK (v1.4.1) reverting the batching envelope change and adding integration tests for model_hint propagation. target: 6 hours.

nidhi: also adding server-side guard: reject batched envelopes missing per-item model hints with a clear error instead of silently falling back. deploy in 2 hours.

ryan_m: additional note: for Go and Python SDKs, audit whether they have similar batching changes. I saw a Go PR that concatenates inputs but forgot to include model per item — might be a cross-SDK issue.

support-bot: Action items created: SVC-1124 (JS hotfix), SVC-1125 (server guard), SVC-1126 (SDK audit for Go/Python).

alex_s: customer mitigation steps (summary):
- temporarily set batchSize=1 or disable client batching
- use direct HTTP curl if urgent
- increase SDK timeout to avoid partial retries that surface mismatch errors
- confirm your logs for request_id and region and forward them to support

customer_jones: thanks, applying batchSize=1 now. will confirm after a few requests.

(30m later)

customer_jones: update: after setting batchSize=1 the errors stopped. thanks. any ETA on release?

eng-ml: hotfix published: @redwood-embeddings-js v1.4.1 with the batching bugfix and extra test coverage. Please upgrade and remove the batchSize=1 workaround. changelog: fix(model): preserve model_hint for all batched items.

customer_jones: upgraded and verified — returning 1536-dim vectors. huge help, appreciate the quick turnaround :rocket:.

alex_s: closing loop — eng-ml to follow up with a postmortem blameless doc (SVC-1124). support will mark ticket RT-4572 resolved but keep monitoring for 24h.

nidhi: follow-up tasks for devex: add an example to the SDK README on how to explicitly set batchSize and timeout and a caveat section about model routing.

ryan_m: also adding an automated QA test that runs an end-to-end embedding with batch>1 and asserts response dims==model.expected_dim.

support-bot: Ticket RT-4572 resolved by customer confirmation. Monitoring open for 24h.
